newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JONES SENDS WARNING TO 100 METRES RIVAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES SENDS WARNING TO 100 METRES RIVAL.

text.p: American sprint champion Marion Jones warned her rivals she is the woman to beat with a formidable victory in the 100 metres semifinals on the second day of the world championships on Sunday.

The 21-year-old former basketball player, bidding for her first major title here, won the race with plenty to spare in 10.94 seconds. She was slowing down as she crossed the line while her main rival Merlene Ottey had to work hard to take second.

Jamaican veteran Ottey, who has won a record 13 world championship medals but who is still seeking her first 100 gold, took second in 11.08 with Sevatheda Fynes of the Bahamas and American Inger Miller taking the other places in Sunday's final from the heat.
"Three down and one to go. I felt good out of the blocks, " Jones said. "I am ready to wrap it up tonight."
Ukraine's Zhanna Pintussevich, who ran powerfully in Saturday's first two rounds, won the first semifinal in 11.10 but was pushed all the way by France's Christine Arron who took second in 11.13.
In a tight finish for the other key places in the final German Melanie Paschke and American Chryste Gaines took third and fourth in 11.34 and 11.35 respectively.
